legacy_record.justification: SPEI-12 is the standard metric for agricultural drought, capturing cumulative moisture deficit over a 12-month window. It is directly relevant to agroforestry systems where tree establishment and early canopy development are sensitive to prolonged dry periods. Brandt et al. (2015) and Mendonça et al. (2022) use precipitation/aridity exposure as the primary climate hazard layer in CSA/agroforestry suitability frameworks. Drought is the dominant climate barrier for agroforestry adoption in semi-arid Africa and South Asia (Ahmad et al. 2020).

audit.quantity_and_unit: SPEI-12 / unitless
audit.temporal_statistic: Monthly 12-month accumulated anomaly; long-term reducer unresolved
audit.valid_spatial_support: Native 0.5 degree (~55 km), not resampled 1 km
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Reverse direction: lower SPEI is drier. T1 mean/trend is not T5 frequency/severity. Event classes can be proposed; climatological frequency cutoffs remain empty.

dataset_records.citation: Vicente-Serrano, S.M. et al. (2010). A Multiscalar Drought Index Sensitive to Global Warming: The Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index. Journal of Climate, 23(7), 1696–1718.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Extract SPEI-12 (12-month accumulation window) for drought risk. Compute mean and trend over 1981–2010 baseline. Bilinearly resample to 1 km for overlay.
dataset_records.limitations: Very coarse native resolution (0.5°). Misses sub-regional drought heterogeneity. PET estimation method affects values. Not for: Farm-level drought monitoring; flash drought detection
dataset_records.description: Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index, global ~55 km, monthly 1901-present.

legacy_record.justification: Extreme heat events damage tree seedlings and reduce photosynthetic efficiency. Yadav et al. (2024) use Tmax_May (hottest pre-monsoon month) and Tmax_Jan as key inputs to AHP-based agroforestry suitability in Punjab. BIO5 (max temp of warmest month) is the most agriculturally relevant temperature extreme for heat stress assessment.

audit.quantity_and_unit: BIO5 / degrees Celsius after verified scaling
audit.temporal_statistic: Maximum temperature of warmest month; 1981–2010 climatology
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Related to T5 heat concern but BIO5 is not extreme-day frequency. Agree quantity, population/crop/livestock endpoint and scaling before common representative.

dataset_records.citation: Karger, D.N. et al. (2017). Climatologies at high resolution for the earth's land surface areas (CHELSA). Scientific Data, 4, 170122.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Resample to 1 km COG. CHELSA-BIOCLIM+ Version 1.2 used by Yadav et al. (2024) for agroforestry suitability in Punjab. Use Bio1 (Annual Mean Temp), Bio12 (Annual Precipitation), Tmax_Jan, Tmax_May.
dataset_records.limitations: Statistical downscaling from ERA5; may show artefacts in complex terrain. Less validated over Africa and Central Asia. Not for: Short-term weather forecasting or sub-field precision agriculture
dataset_records.description: Bias-corrected high-resolution global bioclimatic variables, climatology 1981-2010 (~1 km).

legacy_record.justification: Heavy rainfall events cause soil waterlogging and root damage in agroforestry systems, particularly in low-lying and floodplain areas. Castle et al. (2025) treat flood hazard as a suitability constraint for agroforestry in the US Midwest, excluding floodplain areas. Baldwin et al. (2022) integrate flood inundation as a key exposure layer. BIO13 (wettest month precipitation) is a practical proxy for flood-generating rainfall intensity at 1 km resolution.

audit.quantity_and_unit: BIO13 wettest-month precipitation / mm
audit.temporal_statistic: 1981–2010 climatological wettest month
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Precipitation is not flood depth, extent or exposed assets. Reject automatic equivalence with T5 flood hazard; replace proxy or relabel through review.

dataset_records.citation: Karger, D.N. et al. (2017). Climatologies at high resolution for the earth's land surface areas (CHELSA). Scientific Data, 4, 170122.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Resample to 1 km COG. CHELSA-BIOCLIM+ Version 1.2 used by Yadav et al. (2024) for agroforestry suitability in Punjab. Use Bio1 (Annual Mean Temp), Bio12 (Annual Precipitation), Tmax_Jan, Tmax_May.
dataset_records.limitations: Statistical downscaling from ERA5; may show artefacts in complex terrain. Less validated over Africa and Central Asia. Not for: Short-term weather forecasting or sub-field precision agriculture
dataset_records.description: Bias-corrected high-resolution global bioclimatic variables, climatology 1981-2010 (~1 km).

legacy_record.justification: Agricultural land is the primary exposure element for climate risks affecting agroforestry investment. Higher proportions of cropland and pasture indicate greater exposure of rural livelihoods to climate hazards. Used implicitly or explicitly across the majority of the 23 agroforestry stocktake papers as the base land-use layer defining the eligible intervention space.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Cropland area fraction / fraction
audit.temporal_statistic: WorldCover 2021 snapshot
audit.valid_spatial_support: 10 m classes aggregated to declared support
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Define cropland class and denominator/mask; grassland and sparse vegetation are not evidence of agriculture or pasture. Categorical source requires explicit fraction derivation; exposure is not hazard.

dataset_records.citation: Zanaga, D. et al. (2022). ESA WorldCover 10m 2021 v200. Zenodo.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Reclassify to agricultural mask (cropland, grassland, sparse vegetation) to define eligible agroforestry conversion area. Exclude built-up, water bodies, bare soil with high salinity. Aggregate to 100m or 1km for pipeline. Used as LULC base by multiple AF studies.
dataset_records.limitations: Mixed-pixel confusion in fragmented agricultural landscapes. Annual snapshot — does not capture seasonal cultivation. Accuracy lower in arid landscapes and under cloud cover. Not for: Crop-type mapping; sub-field land use classification
dataset_records.description: ESA WorldCover 10 m global land-cover map (2021), Sentinel-1/2 derived 11-class classification.

legacy_record.justification: Higher rural population density amplifies the human exposure dimension of climate risk and also signals greater potential beneficiary reach of agroforestry investments. Applied as a shared variable — used in risk (exposure component) and retained in opportunity space (beneficiary reach) with double_count_risk guard set to 'shared'.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Rural population count or density / persons or persons/km2
audit.temporal_statistic: 2020 snapshot; rural mask period required
audit.valid_spatial_support: 100 m population estimates; retain census limitations
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Same underlying population concern as T5 descriptor. Define count-to-density conversion and rural mask. Do not restore scoring through T2 while T5 is descriptor.

dataset_records.citation: WorldPop (2020). Global High Resolution Population Denominators Project - Funded by The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (OPP1134076). University of Southampton.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Aggregate to 1 km for pipeline. Use as proxy for population exposure in climate risk and as denominator for opportunity space poverty metrics.
dataset_records.limitations: Constrained model relies on settlement/building footprint mapping — may undercount nomadic/dispersed rural populations. Accuracy varies with census quality of input data. Not for: Individual household targeting; electoral boundary analysis
dataset_records.description: Global gridded population estimates at 100 m for the year stated (WorldPop).

legacy_record.justification: Soils with low organic carbon and high sand content are more sensitive to drought and erosion, and agroforestry systems on such soils are more vulnerable to climate shocks. Ahmad & Goparaju (2017) and Haile (2024) identify nutrient availability and soil quality as primary sensitivity indicators for agroforestry viability. Low-nutrient capital soils exhibit high sensitivity in the CrossBoundary fragile_gains archetype.

audit.quantity_and_unit: SOC concentration and sand content / g/kg and percent
audit.temporal_statistic: Static prediction; explicit soil depth/statistic
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: No composite definition or direction: low SOC and high sand are different signals. Not equivalent to erosion rate. Specify metric/depth/uncertainty; avoid duplicate soil proxies.

dataset_records.citation: Poggio, L. et al. (2021). SoilGrids 2.0: producing soil information for the globe with quantified spatial uncertainty. SOIL, 7, 217–240.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Select property asset and source-compatible depth explicitly; apply provider unit conversion once. Do not assume a 0-30 cm composite or a fixed 1 km output grid. Keep topsoil/subsoil and concentration/stock distinct; record aggregation and uncertainty.
dataset_records.limitations: Prediction uncertainty is high in data-sparse regions (much of sub-Saharan Africa). Point observations biased toward accessible areas. Temporal static — does not capture land-use change effects on soil. Not for: Precision soil management at plot level; nutrient management plans without ground-truthing
dataset_records.description: Global digital soil mapping (250 m) of physical and chemical soil properties at six depths.

legacy_record.justification: Access to roads and markets enables farmers to access inputs, extension services, and output markets — all of which increase adaptive capacity to climate shocks. Remoteness (high road distance) reduces adaptive capacity. Chuma et al. (2021) use distance to roads as an agroforestry suitability criterion. Castle et al. (2025) include infrastructure connectivity as a social-ecological suitability layer.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Distance to mapped road / m
audit.temporal_statistic: 2024 OSM snapshot in T1
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Raw distance increases remoteness; negative_risk label conflates capacity with distance. Travel time is related, not identical. Soft enabling condition belongs in separate operational risk/context; no automatic M4 entry.

dataset_records.citation: OpenStreetMap contributors (2024). OpenStreetMap. www.openstreetmap.org.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Compute Euclidean distance to nearest road of any class. Used by Chuma et al. (2021) as infrastructure accessibility layer. Apply 5km threshold as moderate accessibility constraint for agroforestry market access. is_scenario_candidate = true (road investment can change this).
dataset_records.limitations: OSM coverage quality is highly variable in rural sub-Saharan Africa, Central Asia, and remote tropical regions — significant under-mapping in key project areas. Validate against national road datasets where possible. Not for: Routing or logistics planning; travel-time modelling without validation
dataset_records.description: OpenStreetMap global road network vector lines, multiple admin levels.

legacy_record.justification: Future drought risk under SSP2-4.5 is the key forward-looking hazard for long-horizon agroforestry investments. Mendonça et al. (2022) incorporate future climate projections (precipitation anomaly 2050) as a driver of agroforestry prioritisation. Given agroforestry establishment periods of 5–15 years, decisions made today need to account for mid-century climate conditions.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Future SPEI-12 / unitless (not supplied)
audit.temporal_statistic: SSP2-4.5, 2041–2070; common baseline fit required
audit.valid_spatial_support: Unresolved; CHELSA ~1 km does not establish SPEI support
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Dataset is CHELSA bioclim, with no SPEI derivation or ensemble/baseline fit. No comparable baseline/future classifications until derived quantity is verified. Scenario alternative, not extra weighted concern.

dataset_records.citation: Karger, D.N. et al. (2023). CHELSA-W5E5: Daily 1 km meteorological forcing data for climate impact studies. Earth System Science Data, 15, 2445–2464.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Use delta-change approach relative to baseline. Clip to project AOI. Ensemble mean of available CMIP6 GCMs preferred.
dataset_records.limitations: Ensemble spread is wide in tropical regions. Precipitation projections carry higher uncertainty than temperature. Not for: Single-GCM deterministic planning; local infrastructure design
dataset_records.description: CHELSA bioclimatic variables under SSP2-4.5 around 2050 (CMIP6 ensemble downscaled).

legacy_record.justification: High runoff depth is simultaneously a flood hazard indicator AND the primary measure of water harvesting opportunity. Terencio et al. (2017) weight overflood risk as a suitability barrier. Abd-el-Kader et al. (2023) and Ahmad et al. (2024) explicitly target high-runoff zones as RWH sites for flood-risk adaptation. Shared variable - used in risk (flood hazard) and opportunity space (RWH potential).

audit.quantity_and_unit: Event runoff depth / mm (not supplied)
audit.temporal_statistic: Design event and antecedent conditions undefined
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: T1 ID says SCS-CN composite but name/URL/asset describe HydroSHEDS boundaries. Runoff generation is not inundation depth; routing and event specification missing.

dataset_records.dataset_name: HydroSHEDS Watershed Boundaries and River Network
dataset_records.citation: Lehner, B. et al. (2008). New global hydrography derived from spaceborne elevation data. Eos, Transactions AGU, 89(10), 93-94.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Use HydroBASINS level 8-10 for sub-watershed delineation context. Stream order used as a primary RWH site-type discriminator: first/second-order streams suit check dams and gully plugs; third/fourth-order streams suit percolation tanks; larger streams suit small dams. Kumar et al. (2018) and Singh et al. (2016) use stream order as a primary MCDA criterion.
dataset_records.limitations: Derived from 3-arc-second SRTM; misses ephemeral channels in flat arid terrain. Resolution insufficient for first-order gully mapping. Not for: Detailed gully morphometry; flash flood routing
dataset_records.description: Composite SCS curve-number runoff potential surface combining land-cover and hydrologic soil group.

legacy_record.justification: High inter-annual rainfall variability exposes rain-fed systems to erratic water availability, increasing the value of storage. Mahmoud et al. (2014) use rainfall variability in RWH site prioritisation. Khan et al. (2022) quantify climate-driven reductions in reliable rainfall as a key exposure driver.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Interannual precipitation coefficient of variation / percent (proposed)
audit.temporal_statistic: Annual/seasonal totals over declared multi-year period
audit.valid_spatial_support: True CHIRPS ~5 km if chosen; current T1 contradictory
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: T1 ID/description say CHIRPS but name/URL/version are WorldClim climatology; T1 explicitly says no interannual variability. Hazard variability is not exposure. Rebind time series and define season/zero-mean handling.

dataset_records.citation: Fick, S.E. & Hijmans, R.J. (2017). WorldClim 2: new 1km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. International Journal of Climatology, 37(12), 4302-4315.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Rainfall is the second most frequent input variable (38 of 85 papers). Extract mean annual precipitation and wet-season monthly totals. Use for SCS-CN runoff depth calculation combined with HSG soil map. Buraihi & Shariff (2015) use projected precipitation to assess future RWH viability under climate change.
dataset_records.limitations: 30-year climatological mean; interannual variability not captured. Resolution too coarse for localised orographic precipitation in complex terrain. Not for: Flood frequency analysis; design-storm estimation for dam sizing
dataset_records.description: Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Stations, ~5 km daily precipitation 1981-present.

legacy_record.justification: High-permeability soils have low water retention, making systems more sensitive to drought. Vema et al. (2019) use soil permeability as a direct suitability input. Bera & Mukhopadhyay (2023) include soil texture as a key sensitivity variable.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Hydraulic conductivity or water retention / unresolved
audit.temporal_statistic: Static prediction; explicit depth/statistic
audit.valid_spatial_support: SoilGrids 250 m covariates; derived product unresolved
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Texture is not measured permeability; no pedotransfer function supplied. High permeability can aid infiltration but reduce storage: endpoint and direction unresolved; do not force monotonic thresholds.

Temporal static — does not capture land-use change effects on soil. Not for: Precision soil management at plot level; nutrient management plans without ground-truthing

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Long-term SPEI-based drought severity / frequency — areas where dry climatic stress is high.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Drought event frequency or accumulated severity / unresolved
audit.temporal_statistic: Long-term baseline and reducer unresolved; future flag is not a binding
audit.valid_spatial_support: SPEI native 0.5 degree, not VONT 5 km
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Shares drought concern with both T2 SPEI entries. Source event severity classes do not calibrate a long-term frequency map. Keep event-rule candidate separate from current T5 activation.

dataset_records.citation: Vicente-Serrano, S.M. et al. (2010). A Multiscalar Drought Index Sensitive to Global Warming: The Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index. Journal of Climate, 23(7), 1696–1718.

dataset_records.limitations: Very coarse native resolution (0.5°). Misses sub-regional drought heterogeneity. PET estimation method affects values. Not for: Farm-level drought monitoring; flash drought detection

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Return-period flood depth/extent — areas exposed to riverine/pluvial flooding.

audit.quantity_and_unit: River flood depth at fixed return period / m
audit.temporal_statistic: Baseline, return period explicit; future dataset missing
audit.valid_spatial_support: JRC product support must be verified by edition
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: T5 includes pluvial wording; T1 is river only. BIND requests 100-year but URL names rp50. Return period, protection assumptions, domain/dry-cell meaning and actual asset must agree.

ontology_records.label: Flood hazard (return-period flood depth/extent)
ontology_records.comment: Layer choice deferred — FATHOM, JRC, WRI Aqueduct. Pilot-time decision.

binding_records.fitness_note: JRC Global Flood Hazard 100-year return period as default. WRI Aqueduct + FATHOM (proprietary) considered, JRC chosen for open + global + grid.

dataset_records.dataset_name: JRC Global Flood Hazard Maps (Dottori et al. 2016)
dataset_records.citation: Dottori, F., Salamon, P., Bianchi, A., Alfieri, L., Hirpa, F. A., & Feyen, L. (2016). Development and evaluation of a framework for global flood hazard mapping. Advances in Water Resources, 94, 87-102.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Pick return-period band (100y default for scoping); model assumes existing flood protection per FLOPROS.
dataset_records.limitations: River flooding only — pluvial/urban + coastal flooding need separate layers (e.g. WRI Aqueduct Coastal). Hydrological-model uncertainty in data-sparse basins.
dataset_records.description: JRC global river-flood hazard maps — return-period flood depth grids (e.g. 100-year, 500-year) at ~30 arc-second (~1 km).

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Frequency of extreme-heat days (Tmax or heat-index) — heat-stress exposure for crops, livestock and labour.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Extreme heat frequency / days/year
audit.temporal_statistic: Threshold and daily series period missing; future dataset unresolved
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: VONT days/year conflicts with BIND BIO5 temperature. BIO5 cannot yield extreme-day frequency. Related T2 entry shares concern but not numeric rule.

binding_records.fitness_note: CHELSA BIO5 = max temperature of warmest month — proxy for heat-stress exposure; multi-band asset, band-resolved.

dataset_records.citation: Karger, D.N. et al. (2017). Climatologies at high resolution for the earth's land surface areas (CHELSA). Scientific Data, 4, 170122.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Resample to 1 km COG. CHELSA-BIOCLIM+ Version 1.2 used by Yadav et al. (2024) for agroforestry suitability in Punjab. Use Bio1 (Annual Mean Temp), Bio12 (Annual Precipitation), Tmax_Jan, Tmax_May.
dataset_records.limitations: Statistical downscaling from ERA5; may show artefacts in complex terrain. Less validated over Africa and Central Asia. Not for: Short-term weather forecasting or sub-field precision agriculture
dataset_records.description: Bias-corrected high-resolution global bioclimatic variables, climatology 1981-2010 (~1 km).

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: RUSLE-class soil-erosion risk — where soil-conservation NbS would have the largest mitigation effect.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Annual soil loss / t/ha/year (proposed)
audit.temporal_statistic: Modelled long-term mean; period unspecified
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: No T5 dataset or BIND; VONT suggests SoilGrids, which is not erosion rate. Require complete erosion model factors/validation; do not infer avoidable loss from baseline loss.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: FAO GSOCseq-style additional-SOC potential — where NbS would deliver the largest carbon co-benefit.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Additional SOC accumulation / t C/ha/year (proposed)
audit.temporal_statistic: Explicit management scenario versus baseline and horizon
audit.valid_spatial_support: GSOCseq support if selected; existing GSOCmap 1 km
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: T5 potential is bound to stock (GSOCmap). Stock cannot become additional sequestration by inversion. VONT names fao_gsocseq but T1 lacks that ID. Define potential/benefit interpretation and management counterfactual.

dataset_records.dataset_name: FAO Global Soil Organic Carbon Map (GSOCmap) v1.6.1
dataset_records.citation: FAO & ITPS (2018). Global Soil Organic Carbon Map (GSOCmap) v1.6.1. Technical Report. FAO, Rome.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Use as carbon co-benefit layer in opportunity space. Mendonça et al. (2023) use SOC sequestration potential as an agroforestry prioritisation criterion. Kiziridis et al. (2026) map silvopastoral carbon sequestration. Complement with FAO GSOCseq for sequestration rate.
dataset_records.limitations: Country submissions vary in quality and methodology. National and sub-national SOC maps (where available) should be used in preference. Not for: Carbon crediting baselines without country-specific validation; REDD+ baseline setting
dataset_records.description: FAO Global Soil Organic Carbon map — country-validated 1 km topsoil (0-30 cm) SOC stocks.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Biodiversity Intactness Index (BII, Newbold et al. 2016) at ~1 km global. Use (1 − BII) as priority: lower-intactness pixels surface as higher concern. KBA polygons recommended as supplementary high-priority binary flag.

audit.quantity_and_unit: BII intactness / verified proportion or percent
audit.temporal_statistic: Model edition 2016; underlying reference period unrecorded
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Low intactness may indicate restoration need, not conservation importance. Agree objective before inversion; do not treat KBA binary status as same quantity. No defensible three-cutoff mapping identified.

ontology_records.label: Biodiversity priority (layer TBD)
ontology_records.comment: BII (Newbold et al. 2016) chosen as canonical layer. KBA polygons recommended as supplementary binary flag (vector overlay outside T5).

binding_records.fitness_note: BII (Newbold et al. 2016). Global 1 km. Use (1 - BII) as priority.

dataset_records.citation: Newbold, T., Hudson, L. N., Arnell, A. P., Contu, S., De Palma, A., Ferrier, S., ... & Purvis, A. (2016). Has land use pushed terrestrial biodiversity beyond the planetary boundary? A global assessment. Science, 353(6296), 288-291.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: BII is a 0-100 (or 0-1) intactness index — invert if framing biodiversity_priority as 'higher = more concern' (i.e. priority = 1 - intactness, so lowest-intactness areas surface).
dataset_records.limitations: Modelled (PREDICTS database); systematic uncertainty in under-sampled biomes. Doesn't capture rare-species hotspots — pair with KBA polygons as a binary high-priority flag.
dataset_records.description: Global Biodiversity Intactness Index — modelled remaining proportion of local biodiversity intactness vs an undisturbed baseline, ~1 km global gridded surface.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Downstream water-quality degradation risk (nutrient and sediment loading, thermal stress to aquatic systems) — where riparian, wetland and soil-conservation NbS would have the largest water-quality effect. No scoping-grade global layer yet: BIND requires_upload (national water-quality monitoring) or a nutrient/sediment-export proxy.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Nutrient, sediment or thermal stress / metric-specific
audit.temporal_statistic: Monitoring statistic and season unresolved
audit.valid_spatial_support: Catchment/monitoring reach or admin support unresolved
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: T5 has no dataset; no actual VONT or BIND row despite prose claiming requires_upload. Distinct constituents cannot share thresholds. Need explicit endpoint and downstream routing.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Composite water-stress index — exposure to agricultural / human water-availability constraints.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Aqueduct BWS demand/available renewable supply / fraction
audit.temporal_statistic: Aqueduct 4.0 baseline, 1979–2019 input; annual weighted statistic
audit.valid_spatial_support: HydroBASINS 6; polygon intersections do not add information
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: T5 calls composite; BWS is one ratio. T1 grid/1 km label conflicts with basin support. Official GEE FeatureCollection available. Five source categories plus arid status do not directly yield four method classes; zero/none and endpoints require decision.

binding_records.fitness_note: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 baseline water-stress index. Basin/admin1 granularity.

dataset_records.citation: Kuzma, S., Saccoccia, L., & Chertock, M. (2023). 25 Countries, Housing One-quarter of the Population, Face Extremely High Water Stress. World Resources Institute (Aqueduct 4.0).
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Use the baseline-water-stress (BWS) layer; SSP scenarios available for future projections.
dataset_records.limitations: Basin/admin1 granularity; not pixel-level.
dataset_records.description: World Resources Institute Aqueduct 4.0 baseline water-stress index — ratio of withdrawals to renewable supply, at HydroSHEDS basin level + admin1.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: WB PIP subnational poverty headcount — concentration of rural poor.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Poverty headcount share / percent
audit.temporal_statistic: Survey year, poverty line and PPP vintage required
audit.valid_spatial_support: Actual admin1+ survey support; verify country availability
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: PIP label does not prove rural subnational observations. Need exact series/geography/denominator. Population allocation cannot manufacture within-admin poverty variation; national-only values are flags.

binding_records.fitness_note: WB PIP subnational poverty headcount at admin1 (admin2 where available).

dataset_records.dataset_name: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform — Subnational Poverty Estimates
dataset_records.citation: World Bank (2024). Poverty and Inequality Platform (PIP). World Bank Group, Washington DC.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Interpolate to raster using admin boundary weights and WorldPop population density. Combine with spatial poverty maps (e.g. CGIAR CELL5M poverty layers) for higher-resolution estimates.
dataset_records.limitations: Sub-national resolution limited to admin-1 or -2 in most countries. Survey years vary. Does not capture within-admin spatial variation. Not for: Household targeting; beneficiary selection for project implementation
dataset_records.description: World Bank PIP subnational poverty headcount estimates at admin-1 (admin-2 where available).

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Share of rural households food-insecure (IPC phase / FIES / months of hunger). Split from rural poverty 2026-10-23: food security is its own benefit stream, not a poverty proxy. Scoping layer choice deferred (BIND requires_upload until chosen).

audit.quantity_and_unit: Food-insecure share / percent; IPC phase is separate ordinal quantity
audit.temporal_statistic: Survey/analysis period and severity definition required
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: No VONT/BIND/T5 dataset. IPC phase, FIES prevalence and hunger months are non-equivalent. Keep separate from poverty; choose one measure before thresholds.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Shortfall vs attainable productivity for the dominant farming system. Per-system metric resolved via BIND (yield gap / NPP gap / mixed).

audit.quantity_and_unit: (Attainable minus actual)/attainable production / percent (proposal)
audit.temporal_statistic: Common period, management and attainable benchmark
audit.valid_spatial_support: Per farming system; source support unresolved
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Six BIND rows all require upload. Yield and NPP are not interchangeable; mixed-system combination lacks weights/units. No default cutoffs; attainable zero and negative gaps need policy.

ontology_records.label: Production gap vs attainable productivity
ontology_records.comment: Per-farming-system metric resolved via BIND: yield-gap (GAEZ/MapSPAM) for cropping; NPP gap for rangeland; mixed where applicable. Livestock side often requires_upload.

binding_records.fitness_note: Cropping-rainfed yield gap — GAEZ v4 attainable-vs-actual or MapSPAM-derived; pilot binding to be uploaded.
Cropping-irrigated yield gap — GAEZ v4 irrigated attainable-vs-actual; pilot binding to be uploaded.
Mixed systems: composite of crop yield gap and livestock-productivity gap; livestock side often thinner — flag for upload.
Rangeland NPP gap (e.g. MODIS NPP vs CASA potential); livestock side often thinner — requires_upload by default.
Agro-pastoral composite (cropping yield-gap + NPP-gap) — pilot upload.
Tree-perennial production gap — MapSPAM-based attainable for the perennial; per-crop binding (cocoa/coffee/etc.) preferred.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Share of livelihoods / employment dependent on the agricultural sector — where ag-NbS shocks/benefits hit hardest.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Agricultural employment share / percent
audit.temporal_statistic: Annual selected series; year missing
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: National ILO series cannot differentiate within-country hotspots. Employment share is not household livelihood dependence. Obtain admin1+ data or retain national qualified flag; no raster upscaling claim.

binding_records.fitness_note: ILOSTAT 'employment in agriculture (% of total)' admin0 indicator. Subnational requires_upload.

dataset_records.citation: ILO (2024). ILOSTAT — Labour Statistics. International Labour Organization, Geneva.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Use 'agricultural employment as % of total employment' as the rural-labour-availability framing; pair with LSMS-ISA for subnational where present.
dataset_records.limitations: Country-level only; subnational variation requires LSMS-ISA or country uploads.
dataset_records.description: International Labour Organization ILOSTAT — labour-force participation, agricultural employment share, wage indicators. Admin0, annual.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: National-level gender-inequity index. Subnational disaggregation requires_upload.

audit.quantity_and_unit: UNDP GII / unitless
audit.temporal_statistic: 2022 per T1; snapshot must be pinned
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Retain T5 priority designation historically; current binding only qualifies national context. No within-country scoring without justified subnational measure; GII is not directly disaggregated by rasterization.

ontology_records.label: Gender inequity index (national flag)
ontology_records.comment: National-flag layer for now. Subnational disaggregation requires_upload.

binding_records.fitness_note: UNDP Gender Inequality Index — national flag. Per T5 spatial-grain rule, surfaces as qualified flag within a country, not hotspot driver.

dataset_records.citation: UNDP (2024). Gender Inequality Index (GII). Human Development Report Office, United Nations Development Programme.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: National-flag layer; subnational disaggregation requires_upload (LSMS, DHS).
dataset_records.limitations: Admin0 only — no subnational variation. Per T5 spatial-grain rule, surfaces as qualified flag, not hotspot driver.
dataset_records.description: UNDP Human Development Report Office Gender Inequality Index — composite of reproductive health, empowerment, labour-market gender gap. Admin0, annual.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Indigenous & community lands within the opportunity space (LandMark + WWF/ICCA). Subnational equity-priority signal — surfaces marginalised communities and triggers FPIC/ESS7 flag for M6 hand-off. Coverage patchy — absence ≠ no IPLC presence.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Mapped Indigenous/community land presence / binary with unknown
audit.temporal_statistic: 2024 catalogue; feature survey/revision dates required
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Rights/safeguard presence is not graded deficit. No three numeric cutoffs. Propose safeguard overlay held outside scoring pending explicit categorical contract decision. Absence of mapped polygon is not confirmed absence.

ontology_records.label: IPLC lands presence
ontology_records.comment: LandMark + WWF/ICCA. Higher presence -> equity priority + FPIC/ESS7 flag for M6 hand-off.

binding_records.fitness_note: LandMark IPLC vector layer. Marks IPLC overlap with M1 opportunity-space mask for equity priority + FPIC/ESS7 flag. Coverage patchy - absence != no IPLC presence.

dataset_records.dataset_name: LandMark — Global Platform of Indigenous & Community Lands
dataset_records.citation: LandMark Consortium (2024). LandMark: Global Platform of Indigenous and Community Lands. World Resources Institute and partners.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Spatial join with AOI; flag overlap as FPIC_REQUIRED for M6 hand-off.
dataset_records.limitations: Coverage is patchy — only countries where IPLC mapping is documented; absence ≠ no IPLC presence.
dataset_records.description: Global vector platform of indigenous and community lands — formal recognition status, customary tenure boundaries.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Rural population density — context for hand-off (how many people are in the hotspot).

audit.quantity_and_unit: Rural population density / persons/km2
audit.temporal_statistic: 2020 snapshot and explicit rural-mask year
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: T2 exposure shares concern, not permission to score. WorldPop counts versus density and constrained/unconstrained asset discrepancy require metadata check; density is not beneficiary count.

dataset_records.citation: WorldPop (2020). Global High Resolution Population Denominators Project - Funded by The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (OPP1134076). University of Southampton.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Aggregate to 1 km for pipeline. Use as proxy for population exposure in climate risk and as denominator for opportunity space poverty metrics.
dataset_records.limitations: Constrained model relies on settlement/building footprint mapping — may undercount nomadic/dispersed rural populations. Accuracy varies with census quality of input data. Not for: Individual household targeting; electoral boundary analysis
dataset_records.description: Global gridded population estimates at 100 m for the year stated (WorldPop).

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Accessibility — travel time to large markets. Context, not a hotspot driver.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Travel time to nearest city >=50,000 people / minutes
audit.temporal_statistic: 2015 surface
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Two equal-ranked global BIND rows target same dataset. Resolve duplicate binding ambiguity. City access is a market proxy, not verified market access; differs from T2 road distance. M2b use remains separate.

ontology_records.label: Travel time to large city/market
ontology_records.aliases: ["market access", "market_access", "travel time to large markets", "accessibility", "travel time"]
ontology_records.comment: Nelson/Weiss accessibility surface — minutes to large town. Maps to WOCAT QM indirect driver 'm' (market access / roads). | market_access (T5/T6/BIND) consolidated here 2026-06-24 #103 — same Nelson/Weiss travel-time surface; synonymous names kept as aliases.

binding_records.fitness_note: Weiss/Nelson 2015 baseline ~1 km global accessibility surface. Travel-time minutes.
Same Nelson/Weiss surface as accessibility_travel_time — re-bound here for the T5 descriptor framing (market connectivity context, not scenario lever).

dataset_records.dataset_name: Global accessibility to cities — Weiss et al. (Nelson) 2018, 2015 baseline
dataset_records.citation: Weiss, D. J., et al. (2018). A global map of travel time to cities to assess inequalities in accessibility in 2015. Nature, 553, 333-336.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Travel time minutes; invert if framing as accessibility (1 / time) for the suitability surface.
dataset_records.limitations: Road network from OSM ~2016; coverage variable in remote regions; not updated for post-2016 infrastructure.
dataset_records.description: Global travel time to the nearest city of 50,000+ inhabitants at ~1 km. Built from road network, terrain, surface friction and city polygons.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Mean farm size / smallholder share — context for which NbS suits the agrarian structure.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Field-size category / categorical; farm area not established
audit.temporal_statistic: Lesiv 2019 edition; observation period to verify
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Field size is not farm size or smallholder status. VONT ha and T5 mean farm size exceed available interpretation. Preserve category, uncertainty and proxy caveat; no priority classification.

ontology_records.label: Mean farm size (smallholder share or median ha)

binding_records.fitness_note: Lesiv et al. 2019 crowdsourced field-size dataset, ~1 km.

dataset_records.dataset_name: Lesiv et al. Global field-size / smallholder share
dataset_records.citation: Lesiv, M., Bayas, J. C. L., See, L., Duerauer, M., Dahlia, D., Durando, N., et al. (2019). Estimating the global distribution of field size using crowdsourcing. Global Change Biology, 25, 174-186.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Use field-size class or smallholder fraction depending on T5 framing.
dataset_records.limitations: Crowdsourced — sampling uneven; complements national agricultural censuses rather than replaces them.
dataset_records.description: Lesiv et al. (2019) global field-size and smallholder-share dataset — derived from crowdsourced photo-interpretation, ~1 km. Field-size class + smallholder fraction.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: MapSPAM-style gridded production value — context on what's at stake economically.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Annual crop value density / USD/ha/year (proposed)
audit.temporal_statistic: MapSPAM 2017 per T1 plus price/base-currency year
audit.valid_spatial_support: ~10 km allocation; crop mix and denominators required
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: Production tonnes/area/yield are not monetary value without crop prices and currency conversion. Verify version/variables; no unsupported price-weighted total or priority score.

ontology_records.label: Agricultural production value (gridded)
ontology_records.comment: Generic MapSPAM-style value layer. Cocoa-specific binding already in T1; this canonical is the multi-crop generalisation.

binding_records.fitness_note: MapSPAM v2.0 summed crop economic value, ~10 km. Weak on tree-perennials — Forest Data Partnership (issue #35) is the supplement.

dataset_records.dataset_name: MapSPAM 2017 v2.0 — global crop production value
dataset_records.citation: International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) (2024). Global Spatially-Disaggregated Crop Production Statistics Data for 2017 Version 2.0. Harvard Dataverse.
dataset_records.preprocessing_notes: Sum economic value across crops for a generic production-value layer; per-crop layers also available.
dataset_records.limitations: Modelled allocation (not surveyed); coarse ~10 km; specific tree-perennial coverage weak (use Forest Data Partnership for cocoa/coffee/palm).
dataset_records.description: IFPRI/IIASA Spatial Production Allocation Model (MapSPAM) v2.0 — gridded crop area, yield, production, value for 42 crops at ~10 km.

legacy_record.ttl_priority_description: Effect on catchment water yield, baseflow and downstream supply; separated from water_stress on 2026-10-16. Local infiltration, soil moisture and dry-season on-farm supply stay under water_stress; what leaves the catchment for downstream users is scored here. Trees can improve the first while reducing the second, and the two must never be averaged into one class. No scoping-grade global layer: BIND requires_upload or a water-balance proxy.

audit.quantity_and_unit: Downstream supply deficit or yield change / unresolved
audit.temporal_statistic: Baseline need versus intervention effect unresolved; season/horizon required
audit.interpretation_and_blocker: No VONT/BIND/dataset. T5 wording is an effect, not baseline need. More yield is not automatically more concern. Keep distinct from local soil moisture/water stress; choose endpoint before any monotonic rule.
